quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: For the table of six: two chicken parm, swap the pasta for salad on one of them; one vegetarian lasagna; and one gluten-free pizza.
quests.correctAnswer: Gluten-Free Pizza, Chicken Parmesan, Vegetarian Lasagna
quests.hint: A big group order stacks several dish types together - track each distinct dish, not the headcount.
quests.explanation: Large group orders can include several different dishes; the substitution on one chicken parm doesn't create an extra item, since 'two chicken parm' is still one dish type.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Split it up: three of us want the burger, no bun for one of them; two want the fish and chips; and could we get an extra portion of mushy peas for the table?
quests.correctAnswer: Mushy Peas, Burger, Fish and Chips
quests.hint: A no-bun variant on one burger doesn't create a new dish type - just track the three real items.
quests.explanation: 'No bun for one of them' modifies a single serving within a larger group count, but it's still the same dish type as the others.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: OK, everyone's ready: Dana wants the salmon but no capers, Priya wants the vegan curry, and the rest of us are splitting two large pizzas - one meat, one veggie.
quests.hint: Four people are mentioned, but only three of today's options are up for selection - notice which one isn't offered as a tile this time.
quests.explanation: Not every real item in a busy group order becomes a selectable option in every question - here, the vegan curry is mentioned but isn't among today's four choices.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: OK, so: I'm vegetarian, my brother's allergic to shellfish, and my mom's gluten-free. I'll have the veggie burger, he'll have the chicken skewers, and she'll have the steak with a gluten-free bun swapped for a lettuce wrap.
quests.hint: Three different dietary needs shape three different dishes for three people.
quests.explanation: This level tracks three separate restrictions across three diners at once - each dish reflects one person's specific need.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Between us: no nuts for me, no dairy for my partner, and no pork for our friend. I'll do the grilled chicken, she'll do the vegan pasta, and he'll do the beef stir-fry.
quests.correctAnswer: Beef Stir-fry, Grilled Chicken, Vegan Pasta
quests.hint: Three restrictions are stated first, then three dishes follow, one per person.
quests.explanation: Stating all the restrictions together before naming the dishes is an efficient way to communicate a complex group's needs at once.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: We're sharing the nachos, but could half be made without cheese, since I'm dairy-free? And I'll have the black bean tacos as my main.
quests.hint: A half-and-half preparation request still describes just one shared starter, plus one individual main.
quests.explanation: A half-modified shared dish is still one order, prepared with a partial accommodation - it doesn't split into two separate menu items.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Since I'm vegan, could the burrito bowl have tofu instead of chicken, and could you leave off the sour cream? I also just don't like cilantro, so no cilantro either, and a lemonade.
quests.hint: A dietary substitution and two separate preference-based removals all describe the very same bowl.
quests.explanation: This shows dietary need (vegan) and personal taste (disliking cilantro) combining on one dish - both are valid reasons for a modifier.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: I can't have gluten, so could the fish be grilled without the breading? And I'd also prefer it without capers - I'm not really a fan, and a side of steamed vegetables.
quests.correctAnswer: Grilled Fish without Breading, Steamed Vegetables
quests.hint: A necessary dietary change and an optional taste preference both shape the same order.
quests.explanation: Distinguishing between what's medically necessary and what's just a preference isn't required for the order itself - both modifiers apply the same way.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: I'm dairy-free, so the mac and cheese is out for me - but could I get the same sauce made with a plant-based cheese if you have it? Server: We can do that, actually. Customer: Perfect, I'll have that, then, and a sparkling water.
quests.correctAnswer: Sparkling Water, Plant-Based Mac and Cheese
quests.hint: The conditional backup plan becomes irrelevant once the kitchen confirms the modification is possible.
quests.explanation: Setting up a backup plan is smart, but once the preferred option is confirmed as possible, the backup plan is simply never used.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Is the vegan chili available today? Server: Sorry, we sold out an hour ago. Customer: Ah - is there another vegan option? The lentil soup? Perfect, I'll have that, with bread.
quests.hint: An unavailable dietary-friendly dish leads to a second dietary-friendly option, not just any dish.
quests.explanation: When a dietary-suitable dish is unavailable, the natural next question narrows down to other suitable options, not the whole menu.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Customer: Do you have anything gluten-free that isn't just a salad? Server: The grilled salmon with rice works. Customer: That's perfect, actually - I was getting tired of salads. I'll have that, and a lemonade.
quests.hint: The customer expresses mild frustration before accepting a welcome alternative.
quests.explanation: A small aside about being tired of salads adds realistic personality to the exchange without changing what's actually ordered.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Is the vegan burger available? No? What about the veggie wrap - also out? Oh no. OK, then just a big side salad and some fries, I suppose.
quests.hint: Two unavailable options in a row lead to a fallback choice, marked by resignation.
quests.explanation: 'I suppose' shows the final choice isn't the customer's first preference, but it's still the real, final order once two other options failed.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: We're already running late for a movie - is there anything that can come out in under ten minutes? The soup and sandwich combo, both of us, quickly, please, and two waters.
quests.hint: A firm time constraint narrows the order down to the fastest option for both people.
quests.explanation: Time pressure combined with two people ordering the same thing shows how constraints can simplify a final decision.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Server: The kitchen's backed up tonight - starters are taking twenty minutes. Customer: In that case, skip the starter for us and just bring the mains when they're ready: the steak and the salmon.
quests.hint: A kitchen delay leads the customer to skip an entire course rather than wait.
quests.explanation: Adjusting the whole structure of an order in response to a delay is a realistic, practical solution to a timing problem.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Half of us have a train to catch in thirty minutes - could their food come out first? They'll have the sandwiches, and the rest of us, who aren't in a rush, will have the steaks.
quests.hint: The group splits into two timing categories, each with its own dish.
quests.explanation: Splitting a group's timing needs while keeping track of two separate dish choices is a genuinely advanced ordering skill.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the guest's final order.
quests.prompt: Server (rushed): OK go, go, what do you need? Customer: Um - the chicken, no wait, the beef, and a coke, quickly!
quests.hint: A rushed, pressured exchange still contains a clear correction - trust the final word.
quests.explanation: Even under time pressure and with hesitation, the customer's final, corrected choice is what should be tapped.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Server: We're slammed, sorry - quick, what'll it be? Customer: Uh, the special, whatever that is today, and water, tap water's fine.
quests.hint: The customer accepts an unknown dish under time pressure, trusting the label 'special.'
quests.explanation: 'Whatever that is today' shows the customer ordering without full information, purely because of the rushed situation.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Customer: Wait, does the- Server: Sorry, no time, kitchen's closing in two minutes! Customer: OK, OK - the burger, plain, and a coke, quickly!
quests.hint: An attempted question is cut short by real time pressure, so the customer orders without getting an answer.
quests.explanation: Sometimes real time pressure means a clarifying question never gets answered - the customer has to decide anyway.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Server: I'm so sorry, we're completely out of that dish. Customer: Oh, that's totally fine, don't worry about it! I'll just have the pasta instead, and a side salad.
quests.hint: A gracious, reassuring response follows bad news before the actual replacement order.
quests.explanation: Responding warmly to bad news keeps the interaction pleasant, which matters as much as the words of the order itself.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Server: I have to admit, I forgot to put your order in - I'm really sorry. Customer: Oh no, that happens! No big deal - can we just go with the chicken and rice now, please?
quests.hint: The customer forgives a real mistake gracefully before restating the order.
quests.explanation: Reacting kindly to an honest mistake is socially appropriate and keeps the situation calm for everyone.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the guest's final order.
quests.prompt: Customer: I don't want to make this awkward, but I think we might have been undercharged - we had three mains, not two. It should be the pasta, the salmon, and the steak.
quests.hint: The customer proactively points out an error that benefits them, rather than staying quiet.
quests.explanation: Honestly pointing out an undercharge, even though it costs the customer more, is a socially responsible and realistic choice some diners make.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: I'm vegetarian and the veggie burger's sold out, so is there anything else meat-free? Server: The stuffed peppers. Customer: I'll have those, then, no cheese since I'm also dairy-free today, and a side salad.
quests.hint: An unavailable item, a dietary question, a server suggestion, and a second dietary note all combine before the final order.
quests.explanation: This level combines an unavailability problem with two separate dietary considerations, resolved through a single natural conversation.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Could the salmon be prepared without butter since I'm dairy-free, and could you check if there's a lower-sodium option for the sauce too, since my doctor recommended I watch my salt intake? And a side of steamed vegetables, no added salt.
quests.hint: Two separate health-related requests, from two different reasons, both apply to this order.
quests.explanation: Diners sometimes combine a dietary restriction with a doctor's recommendation - both are legitimate, communicated reasons for a modified order.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Could I get the risotto without dairy? Server: It's made with a cream base throughout, I'm afraid, we can't remove it. Customer: OK, then what about the vegetable stir-fry - is that dairy-free? Yes? Great, I'll have that, with rice.
quests.hint: A failed substitution attempt leads to a completely different dish, confirmed as suitable before ordering.
quests.explanation: When a substitution truly isn't possible, switching to an entirely different dish, after confirming it fits the need, is the practical next step.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: We've got twenty minutes before our show starts, my sister's vegan, and my dad doesn't do spicy - so, quickest vegan thing that's not spicy? Server: The lentil soup. Customer: Perfect, that for her, and I'll have the mild chicken.
quests.hint: Three constraints (time, diet, spice tolerance) are stated together before the server offers one solution.
quests.explanation: Stacking multiple constraints into a single question is an efficient, advanced way to get a fast, suitable recommendation from the server.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: OK, given that half the table's gluten-free and we need to eat fast before the game starts, what's quick and safe for everyone? Server: The rice bowls, all gluten-free, ready in ten. Customer: Let's do that - two rice bowls, and I'll grab a coke.
quests.hint: Two constraints are solved at once by a single dish type the server suggests.
quests.explanation: A well-chosen menu item can sometimes satisfy several constraints simultaneously - here, both the dietary need and the time pressure.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Honestly, there's no single thing that's both nut-free and ready quickly - could we just get the salad, hold the walnuts, even if it takes a couple extra minutes? We don't mind waiting a bit for that one, and two lemonades.
quests.hint: When no option satisfies every constraint perfectly, the group consciously accepts a small trade-off.
quests.explanation: Real decisions sometimes require accepting an imperfect trade-off - the group here knowingly chooses a slight wait over a less safe option.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Big table, sorry in advance: I'm vegan, my husband's gluten-free, the kids just want plain pasta, and we're on a bit of a schedule - could you tell us what can come out fastest that covers all that? Server: The vegetable stir-fry works for you two, and the kids' pasta is always quick.
quests.hint: Several constraints - two diets, kids' preferences, and time - are solved together by the server's single suggestion.
quests.explanation: This level brings together everything from the unit: multiple dietary needs, a group order, and a timing constraint, all resolved in one natural exchange.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: Is the seafood platter available? Sold out? OK - is there a shellfish-free seafood option, since my brother's allergic, that's still quick, since we've got a reservation elsewhere at eight? Server: The salmon, ten minutes. Customer: Perfect, that for him, and the rest of us will have the steaks.
quests.hint: An unavailable dish, an allergy, and a timing constraint all get resolved together before the group's order is finalized.
quests.explanation: This mirrors the most demanding real restaurant situations: unavailability, an allergy, and a hard deadline, worked through in one connected conversation.

quests.instruction: Tap the items to fulfill the customer's order.
quests.prompt: OK, so: two of us are vegetarian and the mushroom risotto's off tonight - what's the fastest meat-free thing, since we're already late? Server: The veggie flatbread, five minutes. Customer: We'll take two of those, and honestly, just tap water for the table, to keep it quick.
quests.hint: Unavailability, a dietary need, and serious time pressure all combine in this final, most demanding level of the unit.
quests.explanation: This final level of the Advanced Scenarios unit requires holding several real constraints in mind at once and following a fast-moving, realistic conversation.
